title: Parasite
review: The tonal shifts work remarkably well, and the class tension keeps building without feeling forced.

title: Interstellar
review: Huge in scale but the emotional core is what keeps bringing me back.

title: Dune: Part Two
review: The audiovisual experience is spectacular, while the political story feels much sharper than the first film.

title: The Social Network
review: A cold, energetic character study with a script that makes conversations feel like action scenes.

title: Whiplash
review: The performances turn a simple teacher-student conflict into something intense and morally uncomfortable.

title: The Matrix
review: Stylish action, memorable world-building, and a premise that remains fun to think about decades later.

title: Everything Everywhere All at Once
review: Not every joke lands for me, but the film earns its emotional payoff by the end.

title: Blade Runner 2049
review: Slow, atmospheric, and gorgeous; the kind of movie where the mood matters as much as the plot.

title: Arrival
review: I love how the central science-fiction idea is inseparable from the film's treatment of memory and time.

title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
review: The visual design is meticulous, but the melancholy underneath the comedy is what stayed with me.

title: Mad Max: Fury Road
review: Extremely simple on paper, but the staging, editing, and visual storytelling make it feel almost effortless.

title: Her
review: A restrained look at intimacy and technology that feels more interesting now than when it was released.

title: Inception
review: The exposition is heavy, but the concept and set pieces are still immensely satisfying.

title: Spirited Away
review: The world is imaginative without over-explaining itself, and almost every scene contains a memorable detail.

title: The Dark Knight
review: The scale is large, but the film works because its conflicts are grounded in clear character choices.

title: Pulp Fiction
review: The structure keeps ordinary conversations entertaining, even when very little is happening on paper.

title: Fight Club
review: There is a lot I like in the filmmaking, though parts of the film work better for me as satire than drama.

title: La La Land
review: The music and production design are lovely, and the ending gives the romance much more weight.

title: The Godfather
review: Nearly every scene deepens the characters or the family dynamics; the pacing feels deliberate rather than slow.

title: The Shawshank Redemption
review: Its emotional beats are familiar, but the execution is so confident that they still land.
